summary: M4 (Claude Code adapter + M3 must-fix) built by kiro-cli: wb verify passes, 139 tests. Confirmed from the official docs that copying a folder into ~/.claude/plugins/parley does NOT load a plugin; it needs a local marketplace + `claude plugin install` (findings in .workbench/tasks/M4/plugin-loading.md). Independent review round 1 still running.
assumptions: M1 (recorded 2026-11-07, fix session): The secret-scan regex thresholds are builder-chosen minimum length heuristics (AWS AKIA +16 chars; ghp_/github_pat_/sk- at 20+ chars; Slack xox*- tokens at 10+ chars; .env SECRET=TOKEN=PASSWORD=API_KEY lines with values of 12+ chars). They may need tightening after real-world false negative/positive feedback; none may ever be relaxed to log the secret value.

M1 (recorded 2026-11-07, fix session): everyone fan-out derives per-recipient idempotency keys as <base key>::<toAgent>; the double-colon separator is a builder choice, and changing it changes which retries dedupe.

M1 (recorded 2026-11-07, fix session): Claim globs (src/core/glob.ts) follow mk-like path-glob semantics without character classes: * matches within one path segment, ** matches across segments (including zero directories for **/), ? matches one non-separator character.

M1 (recorded 2026-11-07, fix session): Retention is keyed on messages.sent_at (PLAN 4.7 'older than 30 days' interpreted relative to send time), agreements.created_at, edits.at, and message-events are deleted with the messages that own them regardless of event time (keeps FKs safe).
M1 (recorded 2026-11-07, fix session): SQLite connections use WAL journal mode and a 5 s busy_timeout by default; concurrent writers wait briefly instead of failing immediately.
M1 (recorded 2026-11-07, fix session): A reply implies read (PLAN 4.3): delivered->replied is allowed and stamps read_at with the replied timestamp; read->replied keeps the earlier read_at.

M1 review round 1 disputed (opencode.json): the default-model change in opencode.json was requested by the user in chat and recorded as human_approved_exceptions in .workbench/tasks/M1/scope.json, but the record was written by an assistant session; the user should confirm the entry (or tell the workbench to forget it) in M2.

M2 (recorded 2026-11-07): MCP server identity defaults to PARLEY_AGENT_ID env, else harness@folder from PARLEY_HARNESS/cwd. Real adapters (M4+) replace this. Tool-definition tokens estimated at chars/4 (project's own cost model) over JSON.stringify of listTools output; budget is 1,500, measured ~518. Agreement recipient is derived as the latest direct message recipient in the thread. Counter-proposal marks the original 'countered' and inserts a new 'offered' row with parent_id. Rules-file text goes out once per inbox session (ctx.rulesTextSent). wait_for_reply_s polls findLatestReplyTo at 25 ms intervals.

[autonomous] 2026-11-07: GLM-5.3-Flash free and DeepSeek/MiMo free hit OpenCode's free usage limit mid-M2 (GLM resets in ~9.7 h). M2 continued in the same OpenCode session on opencode/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-free, the free model that still answered, instead of waiting or paying. Reversible: all work is in git. (Re-added by Claude: the builder's state rewrite dropped it.)

M2 (recorded 2026-11-07, fix session): The serve command itself (the `parley-mcp serve` CLI wiring in src/cli) is deferred to M3; M2 only owns src/mcp/server.ts#serve and its stdio database lifecycle. src/cli is forbidden in M2 and was not touched.

M3 (recorded 2026-11-07, kiro): offered_to nullable-vs-required (M2 follow-up 3) resolved by folding `offered_to TEXT NOT NULL` into the initial schema (migration 1) and dropping the separate nullable migration 2, since the build is pre-release and no production hub.db exists. A fresh db gets the NOT NULL column; no backfill is needed. If any pre-M3 hub.db exists on a machine it must be recreated (acceptable: no release yet).

M3 (recorded 2026-11-07, kiro): serve() returns a ServeHandle { isClosed(), close() } so the stdio close path is observable/testable. Its db close handler is registered before server.connect and also on stdin end/close; server.connect() preserves and chains an existing transport.onclose (verified in the SDK's shared/protocol.js), so the SDK's close handling is kept.

M3 (recorded 2026-11-07, kiro): resolveRepoRoot uses `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` with a cwd fallback and never throws (discovery groups by that path). resolveDbPath is ~/.parley-mcp/hub.db with a PARLEY_DB_PATH override.

M3 (recorded 2026-11-07, kiro): M3 ships only a fake adapter (src/adapters/fake). It owns ~/.parley-fake/config.json with a managed `parley` key, pretty-printed with a trailing newline so a rewrite round-trips exactly, which makes the byte-for-byte uninstall check deterministic. Real harness adapters, their config paths/formats and hook payloads are M4+ (or M3b once the work harness is named) and go in docs/harness-notes.md.

M3 (recorded 2026-11-07, kiro): inbox drain/watch mark messages delivered but never read — read needs its own evidence (PLAN 4.3). inbox watch polls every 2 s in the command wiring; the pure runInboxWatchOnce step is what tests drive.
M3 (recorded 2026-11-07, kiro): The CLI bin entry src/cli/bin.ts exists but the package.json `bin` field and the compiled path are deferred to M12, since there is no build pipeline yet.

M3 (recorded 2026-11-07, kiro): `pnpm run format` (prettier --write .) reformats the whole repo including committed M1/M2 files and docs, because earlier milestones did not run prettier. Formatting is NOT part of `pnpm check` (the verify gate is lint + typecheck + test). That repo-wide churn was reverted to keep the M3 diff scoped; a dedicated formatting pass is left to the human's discretion.

M4 (recorded 2026-11-07, kiro): User-level Claude Code MCP registration is written to ~/.claude.json under the top-level `mcpServers` key (verified against the official MCP scope docs + current third-party guides, NOT the ~/.claude/settings.json file). The plugin lives at ~/.claude/plugins/parley with .claude-plugin/plugin.json, hooks/hooks.json, monitors/monitors.json (under experimental.monitors) and scripts/. Formats verified against code.claude.com/docs 2026-11-07 (docs/harness-notes.md M4 section); no `claude` binary was run.

M4 (recorded 2026-11-07, kiro): Hook logic lives in TypeScript (src/cli/commands/hook-events.ts + hook-payloads.ts); the plugin's shell scripts only pipe stdin JSON into `parley-mcp hook <event>`. A payload carrying agent_id or agent_type is treated as a subagent event and ignored by every handler (PLAN section 6). The Parley agent id is derived as `claude@<basename(cwd)>` from the hook payload's cwd; the monitor derives the same id from its own $PWD because it gets no session_id. These id-derivation and the monitor's parent-pid/stdout-notification behaviour are ASSUMED and must be confirmed in the human's live two-session test.

M4 (recorded 2026-11-07, kiro): Read-evidence from UserPromptSubmit marks a message read when the message id appears in the prompt text; a still-`sent` message seen in the prompt is delivered-then-read so the guarded state machine moves it legally. Whether Claude naturally echoes a delivered message id into its next prompt is unverified; the monitor line includes the id so it can. Fallback: an unechoed message stays `delivered` (intended, PLAN 4.3).

M4 (recorded 2026-11-07, kiro): DoctorReport gained an optional `hooksTrusted: boolean | null`; the Claude Code adapter reports `null` (plugins/monitors need no per-hook trust). The Adapter interface's install(env, dryRun)/method(env) signatures widen PLAN section 6's zero-arg sketch for testability (temp HOME); documented in src/adapters/types.ts. src/adapters/claude-code/fixtures/*.json are synthetic (marked _synthetic:true) until the human captures real anonymised payloads.
